title: Saudia Carry On Baggage Rules and Limits | Saudia
desc: Learn Saudia carry on baggage rules, size, and weight limits to travel comfortably. Prepare your cabin baggage details and fly with Saudia today.
h1: Saudia Carry On Baggage Rules and Limits | Saudia

Saudia Carry-On Baggage Allowance (Cabin Baggage)

Unchecked baggage (carry-on baggage) allowance

A. Cabin Baggage Size, Weight & Allowance by Travel Class

In addition to the free checked baggage allowance, Saudia allows each guest to carry one piece of hand baggage free of charge. The item must fit in a closed overhead rack or under the seat in front of the guest, and must be tagged with a cabin baggage label, according to the following:

Cabin baggage
Class of service Hand baggage allowance No. of pieces Description Weight
First and Business Class One hand bag 1 Maximum dimensions: 56 × 45 × 25 cm (22 × 18 × 10 in) Up to 12 kg
First and Business Class One briefcase 1 Maximum dimensions: 45 × 20 × 35 cm (18 × 8 × 14 in) Up to 9 kg
Guest Class One hand bag or briefcase 1 Maximum dimensions: 56 × 45 × 25 cm (22 × 18 × 10 in) Up to 7 kg

Note:

  • For guests departing from the USA or Canada to Saudi Arabia, only one carry-on item is allowed in all classes, not exceeding 16 lb in weight and 45 in in dimensions.
  • Saudia may determine, for safety, security, or comfort reasons, whether an item may be carried in the cabin or must be checked in.
  • Check-in staff must inform guests connecting on Saudia that free carry-on baggage may not be accepted at connecting stations due to aircraft type variations or limited overhead storage space.

B. Free personal items

Guests may carry one personal item in addition to their cabin baggage, such as a coat, tablet, women’s handbag, stroller or baby cradle, or essential items for guests with disabilities.

Portable Chargers (Power Banks) Travel Guidelines:
  • According to safety regulations, each passenger is allowed to carry a maximum of TWO rechargeable batteries.
  • It is forbidden to recharge portable charging batteries during being onboard or use them for charging other devices.
  • Portable charging batteries must be carried in carry on baggage onboard the aircraft, and it is forbidden to put them in checked baggage.

Notes:

  • For safety reasons, all carry-on baggage on flights arriving to or departing from the USA and UK will be screened, including all electronic devices (smartphones, cameras, laptops, tablets, smartwatches, etc.). Guests may be asked to power on their devices. Devices that cannot be powered on will not be allowed onboard.
  • Guests traveling to or from the USA or UK must ensure their electronic devices are fully charged to avoid restrictions that may prevent carrying them onboard.
  • Saudia does not provide storage lockers for electronic devices and is not responsible for any loss.

Excess baggage charges for sports equipment

  • International flights:

    1. USD 100 applies to items exceeding the approved dimensions of 158 cm (62 in) up to 205 cm (80 in).
    2. An additional USD 67 applies to items between 205 cm (80 in) and 300 cm (118 in), totaling USD 167.
    3. Items exceeding 300 cm (118 in) or weighing more than 32 kg (70 lb) must be transported via Cargo.
    4. For travel to or from Canada, CAD 89 applies per oversized item, totaling CAD 189.

  • Domestic flights:

    1. SAR 100 applies to each piece exceeding the approved dimensions of 158 cm (62 in) up to 205 cm (80 in).
    2. An additional SAR 100 applies to pieces between 205 cm (80 in) and 300 cm (118 in), totaling SAR 200.
    3. Items exceeding 300 cm (118 in) or weighing more than 32 kg (70 lb) must be transported via Cargo.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many kg of cabin baggage is allowed in Saudia?

Passengers traveling on Saudia can generally carry one cabin bag weighing up to 7 kg, subject to the baggage allowance associated with their fare and travel class.

 What is the maximum cabin baggage size on Saudia?

The maximum cabin baggage dimensions allowed on Saudia are 56 × 45 × 25 cm (22 × 18 × 10 inches) for carry-on bags. The baggage must fit in the overhead compartment or under the seat in front of you and comply with the applicable weight allowance based on your travel class.

 What happens if my carry-on baggage exceeds the allowed weight?

If your carry-on baggage exceeds the permitted weight or size limits, it may need to be checked in as additional baggage. Any applicable excess baggage fees will be charged according to the airline's baggage policy and fare conditions.

 What items are restricted in carry-on baggage?

For safety and security reasons, certain items are restricted or prohibited in carry-on baggage. These include:

  • Sharp objects such as knives, scissors, and blades.
  • Flammable materials, including fuels, lighter refills, and certain aerosols.
  • Explosives, fireworks, and hazardous substances.
  • Self-defense items such as pepper spray and stun devices.
  • Tools that could be used as weapons.
  • Liquids, gels, and aerosols exceeding the permitted limit (typically 100ml per container in carry-on baggage).
  • Electronic devices that cannot be powered on during security inspections on applicable routes.

Some restricted items may be accepted in checked baggage, while others are prohibited entirely. Passengers should review the latest baggage regulations before travel to ensure compliance with security requirements.


 What carry-on baggage is allowed on domestic flights?

For guests traveling domestically, in addition to your carry-on baggage, you are allowed to carry on of the following personal items:

  • Handbags or purses.
  • Laptops and tablets.
  • Mobile phones and chargers.
  • Cameras.
  • Coats or jackets.
  • Baby strollers or baby cradles.
  • Essential medical items.
  • Items required for passengers with disabilities.

All items must comply with applicable size, weight, and security regulations. Additional screening may be required for certain electronic devices and personal belongings.


 What carry-on baggage is allowed on international flights?

For guests traveling internationally, in addition to your carry-on baggage, you are allowed to carry on of the following personal items:

  • Handbags or purses.
  • Laptops and tablets.
  • Mobile phones and chargers.
  • Cameras.
  • Coats or jackets.
  • Baby strollers or baby cradles.
  • Essential medical items.
  • Items required for passengers with disabilities.

All items must comply with applicable size, weight, and security regulations. Additional screening may be required for certain electronic devices and personal belongings.
